cr_logical_semantics.scope: Reviewed eight XL-form Boolean CR operations; MCRF and MCRXR are separately reviewed state-transfer forms.
cr_logical_semantics.bit_numbering: crbD, crbA and crbB are architectural CR bit numbers 0 through 31; bit 0 is CR[31] in the HDL vector.
cr_logical_semantics.source_snapshot: Both input bits are read from the pre-instruction CR before the selected destination bit is replaced, including crbD/crbA/crbB aliases.

cr_state_transfer_semantics.scope: Reviewed MCRF and MCRXR only. MCRFS and newer OCRF forms are not aliases and remain outside this bounded slice.

mcrf.expression: CR field crfD = pre-instruction CR field crfS
mcrf.source_snapshot: The complete pre-instruction source field is read before the destination field is replaced, including crfD=crfS.

mcrxr.expression: CR field crfD = {old XER.SO, old XER.OV, old XER.CA, 0}; XER.SO/OV/CA = 0
mcrxr.atomic_ordering: The CR value uses the pre-instruction XER bits; the selected CR write and three XER clears commit atomically.
mcrxr.reserved_bit_3: 601UM Figure 2-7 and Table 2-8 show XER bit 3 reserved zero. The destination field low bit is therefore zero. This bounded state model preserves its backing xer[28] because only architected SO/OV/CA are writable.

multiply_low_semantics.low_word_note: The low 32 result bits are identical for signed and unsigned interpretations; signed interpretation controls only MULLW overflow.
multiply_low_semantics.ca_rule: MULLI and every MULLW form preserve XER.CA.
multiply_low_semantics.record_rule: MULLW Rc=1 writes CR0 from the signed low-word result and the final sticky SO.
multiply_low_semantics.implementation_timing: The bounded IU reserves the documented Table 6-4 maximum: MULLI 3 and MULLW 5 execute cycles, with accepted finish at E+N. The primary source does not map operands to the lower listed counts; operand-dependent silicon selection remains unresolved, so this does not complete P08.

multiply_high_semantics.scope: MULHW and MULHWU with both Rc values and conservative maximum-latency IU reservation; 64-bit multiply forms, lower operand-selected timings, and silicon scheduling equivalence remain outside this bounded slice.
multiply_high_semantics.reserved_oe: The XO-form bit in the OE position is reserved and must be zero; setting it has boundedly undefined encoding behavior and is rejected by this decoder.
multiply_high_semantics.flag_rule: Both families preserve XER.CA, XER.OV, and XER.SO. Rc=1 writes CR0 from the signed interpretation of the 32-bit high-word result and current XER.SO, including MULHWU results whose bit31 is one.
multiply_high_semantics.implementation_timing: The bounded IU reserves the documented Table 6-4 maximum: MULHW 5 and MULHWU 6 execute cycles, with accepted finish at E+N. The primary source does not map operands to the lower listed counts; operand-dependent silicon selection remains unresolved, so this does not complete P08.

divide_unsigned_semantics.scope: DIVWU with all four OE/Rc forms only; remainder production and silicon-identical internal divider organization remain outside this bounded slice.
divide_unsigned_semantics.normal_result: Unsigned 32-bit rA divided by unsigned 32-bit rB, truncated to the unique integer quotient; no remainder is written.
divide_unsigned_semantics.zero_divisor_architecture: rD and CR0 LT/GT/EQ are undefined. OE=1 writes OV=1 and sticky SO; Rc writes CR0.SO from final SO. CA is preserved.
divide_unsigned_semantics.zero_divisor_local_policy: The scaffold returns rD=0 and records EQ when Rc=1. The iterative divider detects rB=0 and substitutes a harmless internal divisor before its fixed iterations. Tests label zero/EQ as local policy rather than an ISA requirement.
divide_unsigned_semantics.flag_rule: On nonzero divisors OE writes OV=0 and preserves sticky SO; Rc classifies the 32-bit quotient as signed for CR0 LT/GT/EQ and records final/current SO. CA is always preserved.
divide_unsigned_semantics.implementation_timing: The bounded RTL uses a synthesizable 16-step radix-4 restoring divider with no division operator in the synthesized quotient path. The nonpipelined IU reserves 20 execute cycles by default for PID7v and 37 when configured for PID6, with accepted finish at E+N. This establishes the bounded divide timing and implementation milestone but does not complete all P08 multiply timing, silicon-internal equivalence, or FPGA timing closure.

divide_signed_semantics.scope: DIVW with all four OE/Rc forms only; 64-bit DIVD, remainder production, and silicon-identical internal divider organization remain outside this bounded slice.
divide_signed_semantics.normal_result: Signed 32-bit rA divided by signed 32-bit rB, with quotient truncated toward zero; no remainder is written.
divide_signed_semantics.exception_architecture: For rB=0 or rA=INT_MIN with rB=-1, rD and CR0 LT/GT/EQ are undefined. OE=1 writes OV=1 and sticky SO; Rc writes CR0.SO from final SO. CA is preserved.
divide_signed_semantics.exception_local_policy: The scaffold returns rD=0 and records EQ when Rc=1 for both exceptional classes. The iterative divider detects both before magnitude iteration and substitutes harmless internal operands. Tests label zero/EQ as local policy rather than an ISA requirement.
divide_signed_semantics.flag_rule: For normal divisions OE writes OV=0 and preserves sticky SO; Rc classifies the signed quotient in CR0 LT/GT/EQ and records final/current SO. CA is always preserved.
divide_signed_semantics.implementation_timing: The bounded RTL uses a synthesizable 16-step radix-4 restoring divider with no division operator in the synthesized quotient path. The nonpipelined IU reserves 20 execute cycles by default for PID7v and 37 when configured for PID6, with accepted finish at E+N. This establishes the bounded divide timing and implementation milestone but does not complete all P08 multiply timing, silicon-internal equivalence, or FPGA timing closure.

lsu_update_semantics.effective_address: D forms use old rA+EXTS(SIMM16); indexed forms use old rA+old rB modulo 32 bits. Update forms never apply rA-or-zero addressing.
lsu_update_semantics.legality: All selected forms require rA!=0. Loads also require rA!=rD. Indexed bit31/Rc is reserved zero. Store aliases rS=rA and rS/rA/rB aliases are legal and use pre-instruction source values.
lsu_update_semantics.atomic_retirement: Successful loads commit loaded rD and EA rA together; successful stores commit EA rA only after the acknowledged external store reaches accepted retirement. Faults and accepted recovery kills suppress the base update with the load destination.
lsu_update_semantics.implementation_scheduling: The scaffold serializes each update instruction with an empty completion queue and blocks younger dispatch through accepted retirement. This makes an architectural second GPR commit safe without adding a second speculative rename allocation; it does not model the 603e two-destination rename/timing behavior.
lsu_update_semantics.external_memory: One aligned word-addressed big-endian request and one response acknowledgement; byte/half lane steering matches the existing bounded lane. Misaligned half/word operations become terminal diagnostics before a request.

supervisor_integration_semantics.selected_program_exception: Only the all-zero instruction is classified as an opt-in illegal-instruction event. Other unsupported or faulting instructions retain the existing diagnostic behavior.
supervisor_integration_semantics.commit_boundary: SC, selected program events, RFI, and SRR writes mutate supervisor state only when their serialized completion entry is accepted at retirement.
supervisor_integration_semantics.trace_boundary: The selected faulting operation reaches an accepted event-token boundary with the completion diagnostic bit cleared; this is not an architectural normal-completion claim. Architectural cause is exposed through SRR1 and the internal exception redirect.
limits: No exception-priority arbiter beyond the selected serialized events
No oldest-fault classification for LSU, FP, translation, trace, external, reset, machine-check, or decrementer events
No architectural exception event field in retire_packet_t
No GPR bank effect for TGPR; nested entry with TGPR active is rejected
Only PR and IP restored control bits affect this bounded core
No privileged SPR selectors beyond SRR0/1 and SPRG0..3

xer_scope.commit: One exact-tag flag owner; full masked replacement only at accepted retirement, with no sticky SO operation for MTSpr.
xer_scope.preservation: Arithmetic and MCRXR preserve byte count; MCRXR transfers SO/OV/CA/zero to the selected CR field and clears only SO/OV/CA.
xer_scope.aliases: SPR1 accepts MFSPR/MFTB under this feature even without timers; other read aliases retain their timer-enabled policy.

sprg_scope.access: MFSpr reads and MTSpr writes all 32 bits; all eight exact selector aliases require supervisor state.
sprg_scope.commit: MTSpr changes one SPRG only when its serialized completion entry is accepted at retirement.
sprg_scope.hard_reset: The core reset input applies the 603e hard-reset value zero to all four SPRGs.
sprg_scope.soft_reset_limit: The standalone core has no distinct soft-reset input; the 603e soft-reset preservation contract is not implemented.

serialization_integration_semantics.dispatch_contract: Serialized dispatch waits for an empty completion queue, idle normal IU/RS, and idle one-outstanding special/memory lane; younger dispatch remains blocked through accepted retirement.
serialization_integration_semantics.isync_commit: Accepted retirement performs a keep-committing-pivot recovery to PC+4, clearing queued prefetched instructions and using fetch obligation drain/refetch semantics.
serialization_integration_semantics.sync_ordering: The serialized one-outstanding transport has completed every older request/response/retirement before SYNC dispatch and prevents younger requests until SYNC retirement.
serialization_integration_semantics.eieio_ordering: The same serialized rule is conservative for this scaffold’s uncached, strictly ordered, one-outstanding data transport; the 603e itself treats EIEIO as a no-op because cache-inhibited accesses are already strictly ordered.
limits: No second-level cache or alternate requester visibility
No general context-changing instruction pipeline model
